ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The left figure is a right isosceles triangle ABC, with the right angle at B, BA vertical, BC horizontal, and the hypotenuse is AC. The two sides of the inscribed square in the figure lie along BA and BC respectively, and the upper-right corner lies on the hypotenuse AC. The right figure is a right isosceles triangle DEF congruent to it, with the right angle at E, DE vertical, EF horizontal, and the hypotenuse is DF. The square in the right figure is tilted, with one side on the hypotenuse DF, and the two endpoints of the opposite side lying on DE and EF respectively. Reasoning: Let the common leg length of the two congruent right isosceles triangles be L. Set up a coordinate system for triangle ABC: B=(0,0), A=(0,L), C=(L,0), so the equation of the hypotenuse AC is x+y=L. Let the side length of the square in the left figure be s. Since it is placed along the two legs, the upper-right corner is (s,s), and it lies on the hypotenuse, so 2s=L. It is known that the square area s^2=15, therefore L^2=(2s)^2=4s^2=60. For triangle DEF, similarly let E=(0,0), D=(0,L), F=(L,0), and the hypotenuse DF is x+y=L. The endpoints of the opposite side of the tilted square in the right figure lie on the two legs respectively; let them be (0,a) and (a,0). This side is parallel to the hypotenuse, and its side length is a√2. Translating in the perpendicular direction gives the other two vertices (a,2a) and (2a,a), and they lie on the hypotenuse x+y=L, so 3a=L, that is, a=L/3. The area of the square in the right figure is (a√2)^2=2a^2=2(L^2/9)=2·60/9=120/9=40/3.

method.method_draft: Coordinate/length route. First read the diagram: in triangle ABC, the shown square is aligned with the right-angle legs BA and BC, with its opposite corner on hypotenuse AC. In triangle DEF, the shown square is tilted; its upper-right side lies along the hypotenuse DF, and its opposite side has endpoints on the two legs DE and EF. From the text, use that ABC and DEF are congruent isosceles right triangles and that the ABC square has area 15. Let the common leg length be L. Put B at (0,0), A at (0,L), C at (L,0), so AC is x+y=L. If the ABC square has side s, its opposite corner is (s,s), so 2s=L. Since s^2=15, get L^2=60. Now put E at (0,0), D at (0,L), F at (L,0). For the tilted square in DEF, let its lower-left side endpoints on the legs be (0,a) and (a,0), so that side is parallel to the hypotenuse. The other two vertices are then (a,2a) and (2a,a), both on x+y=L, giving L=3a. The tilted square side is a√2, so its area is 2a^2=2L^2/9=40/3.

method.method_draft: Area-decomposition route. First read the diagram: ABC contains a square whose sides lie along the two legs from the right-angle vertex B, and DEF contains a tilted square that partitions the triangle into the square plus three surrounding right-isosceles triangles. From the text, the ABC square area is 15 and the two large triangles are congruent. Let the ABC square side be s, so s^2=15. Because the large triangle is isosceles right and the square corner touches the hypotenuse, each leg of ABC is 2s; hence area(ABC)=1/2(2s)(2s)=2s^2=30. Therefore area(DEF)=30. Let the side of the tilted square in DEF be t. From the image placement, the square has one side on the hypotenuse; the small triangle at E has hypotenuse t, so as a 45-45-90 triangle its area is t^2/4. The two remaining corner triangles at D and F are congruent 45-45-90 triangles with legs t, so each has area t^2/2. Thus area(DEF)=t^2 + t^2/4 + 2(t^2/2)=9t^2/4. Set 9t^2/4=30 to get t^2=40/3, the desired square area.

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: The left figure is a right isosceles triangle ABC, with the right angle at B, BA vertical, BC horizontal, and the hypotenuse is AC. The two sides of the inscribed square in the figure lie along BA and BC respectively, and the upper-right corner lies on the hypotenuse AC. The right figure is a right isosceles triangle DEF congruent to it, with the right angle at E, DE vertical, EF horizontal, and the hypotenuse is DF. The square in the right figure is tilted, with one side on the hypotenuse DF, and the two endpoints of the opposite side lying on DE and EF respectively.

Reasoning: Let the common leg length of the two congruent right isosceles triangles be L. Set up a coordinate system for triangle ABC: B=(0,0), A=(0,L), C=(L,0), so the equation of the hypotenuse AC is x+y=L. Let the side length of the square in the left figure be s. Since it is placed along the two legs, the upper-right corner is (s,s), and it lies on the hypotenuse, so 2s=L. It is known that the square area s^2=15, therefore L^2=(2s)^2=4s^2=60.

For triangle DEF, similarly let E=(0,0), D=(0,L), F=(L,0), and the hypotenuse DF is x+y=L. The endpoints of the opposite side of the tilted square in the right figure lie on the two legs respectively; let them be (0,a) and (a,0). This side is parallel to the hypotenuse, and its side length is a√2. Translating in the perpendicular direction gives the other two vertices (a,2a) and (2a,a), and they lie on the hypotenuse x+y=L, so 3a=L, that is, a=L/3. The area of the square in the right figure is (a√2)^2=2a^2=2(L^2/9)=2·60/9=120/9=40/3.
